classification.difficultyReason: Choose a variable and scale one equation to create matching or opposite coefficients, then link elimination with substitution; no change of representation or exceptional case is required.

content.prompt: Solve the simultaneous equations using the elimination method.

answer.worked:
Multiply the first equation by $3$, then subtract it from the second.
$$\begin{align*}3x+3y&=6\\(3x+4y)-(3x+3y)&=7-6\\y&=1\\x+1&=2\\x&=1\end{align*}$$
Check: $1+1=2$ and $3(1)+4(1)=7$.

Multiply the first equation by $2$, then subtract it from the second.
$$\begin{align*}2x-2y&=4\\(2x+3y)-(2x-2y)&=9-4\\5y&=5\\y&=1\\x-1&=2\\x&=3\end{align*}$$
Check: $3-1=2$ and $2(3)+3(1)=9$.

Multiply the first equation by $2$, then add the second.
$$\begin{align*}8x+2y&=2\\(8x+2y)+(3x-2y)&=2-13\\11x&=-11\\x&=-1\\-4+y&=1\\y&=5\end{align*}$$
Check: $4(-1)+5=1$ and $3(-1)-2(5)=-13$.

Multiply the first equation by $3$, then subtract it from the second.
$$\begin{align*}3x-15y&=27\\(3x+2y)-(3x-15y)&=10-27\\17y&=-17\\y&=-1\\x+5&=9\\x&=4\end{align*}$$
Check: $4-5(-1)=9$ and $3(4)+2(-1)=10$.

Multiply the second equation by $5$, then add the first.
$$\begin{align*}-5x+10y&=-5\\(5x-3y)+(-5x+10y)&=-2-5\\7y&=-7\\y&=-1\\-x-2&=-1\\-x&=1\\x&=-1\end{align*}$$
Check: $5(-1)-3(-1)=-2$ and $-(-1)+2(-1)=-1$.

Check: $\frac{108+13}{11}=11$ and $\frac{180-26}{11}=14$.

Multiply the second equation by $2$, then subtract it from the first.
$$\begin{align*}2x-6y&=10\\(2x+5y)-(2x-6y)&=10-10\\11y&=0\\y&=0\\x&=5\end{align*}$$
Check: $2(5)+5(0)=10$ and $5-3(0)=5$.

Multiply the first equation by $2$, then subtract it from the second.
$$\begin{align*}2x-6y&=0\\(2x-4y)-(2x-6y)&=2-0\\2y&=2\\y&=1\\x-3&=0\\x&=3\end{align*}$$
Check: $3-3(1)=0$ and $2(3)-4(1)=2$.

Multiply the second equation by $3$, then add the first.
$$\begin{align*}3x+21y&=15\\(-3x-2y)+(3x+21y)&=4+15\\19y&=19\\y&=1\\x+7&=5\\x&=-2\end{align*}$$
Check: $-3(-2)-2(1)=4$ and $-2+7(1)=5$.
